clue.text: He predicts there'll be a lot of money on the counter

parts.note: a fortune is a very large sum of money
a teller is one who counts, such as a bank cashier counting out notes

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a fortune on a shop or bank counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' reads as a shop surface, but it means a person who counts: a bank teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller claims to foresee the future, so he is someone who predicts.

clue.text: Journeyed round the world, perhaps

parts.note: reads like a traveller's globe-trotting, but describes a satellite circling the Earth in space

explanation.definitionFit: To circle a planet in space is to travel a path round it, as a satellite does.

clue.text: So long, and thanks, thanks again

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
ta again, the same informal British thank you

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave with a gushing double thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British goodbye, the same farewell as 'so long'.

clue.text: A fisherman's actual profit?

parts.note: a business term for profit after costs, read literally as what an angler gains in his mesh

explanation.definitionFit: Profit after all deductions is the figure left over, and a fisherman's catch is literally gained by his mesh.

clue.text: Ring me first when there's a disagreement about leisure

indicators.note: a quarrel placed about other letters encloses them

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: me comes first, placed ahead of the ring in the run

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone told to phone first when there is a row over their days off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring me first' sounds like a phone instruction; 'first' sets the pair in order and 'about' wraps the quarrel round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Time spent away from work is leisure, free hours to oneself.

clue.text: It's risky to go out on this shoot

definitions.text: It's risky to go out on this

explanation.definitionFit: Going out on a limb is the idiom for taking a risk; and a branch or bough growing from a tree is a shoot.

clue.text: Give a subject a title, perhaps

definitions.text: Give a subject a title, perhaps

parts.words: Give a subject a title, perhaps
parts.note: sounds like naming an essay topic, but a monarch's subject is being raised to the peerage

explanation.definitionFit: Raising a person to the peerage confers a rank such as duke or baron on a citizen of the crown.

clue.text: Striking was prevalent when these staffs were employed

definitions.text: Striking was prevalent when these staffs were employed

parts.words: Striking was prevalent when these staffs were employed
parts.note: suggests industrial strikes among employed staff, but describes posts to which people were tied for flogging

explanation.definitionFit: Offenders were tied to such wooden stakes to be flogged, so beating was common wherever they were used.

clue.text: It takes a turn for the better

definitions.text: It takes a turn for the better

parts.words: It takes a turn for the better
parts.note: an idiom for improving, read as a spinning casino device that turns for people placing bets

explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling device spins round while punters (bettors) wager on where the ball lands.

clue.text: Where one lives a little in Panama, for example

indicators.note: a little is put in the hat, sitting inside it

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: Someone staying briefly in the Central American country of Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country but is a straw hat, with A BIT placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or surroundings of a creature.

clue.text: It reminds me repeatedly not to change

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word me appears twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word not is to be changed, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A note left to oneself that keeps nagging not to alter anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' reads as part of the reminder's message, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake serves to recall a person or event, bringing it back to mind.

clue.text: Stop making a lot of money

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of stop are made into a new word

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit earning a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges the four letters of STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots of money is an idiom for a large amount of cash, so pots alone means plenty.

clue.text: The ghost of Shakespeare, some say

definitions.text: The ghost of Shakespeare, some say

parts.words: The ghost of Shakespeare, some say
parts.note: sounds like Hamlet's spectre, but means the ghostwriter some theorists claim wrote the plays

explanation.walkthrough: The Baconian theory holds that the philosopher Francis Bacon secretly wrote Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Some theorists claim the Elizabethan philosopher Francis Bacon was the true, hidden author of the plays.

clue.text: Pronounced fit to be the first murder victim

indicators.note: pronounced means the word for fit is spoken, giving a name with the same sound

parts.note: fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: Someone declared healthy enough to be the opening casualty in a murder mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in the Book of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain slays his brother, the Bible's first killing.

clue.text: High-flier gets a good score on the course

definitions.text: a good score on the course

explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey soars at great heights; and in golf, two under par on one hole is a fine result.

clue.text: Islet plain to all at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of to all are jumbled

explanation.surface: An island is clearly visible to everyone out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the island picture but signals rearranging TO ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a low, flat ring of coral reef enclosing a lagoon, a small flat island.

clue.text: Thoughtful pub holds raffle

indicators.note: the pub holds the raffle, keeping it inside

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a draw is a raffle or lottery

explanation.surface: A local pub is running a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thoughtful' as indrawn is a less common sense: turned inward, introspective.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn describes someone withdrawn into their own reflections, absorbed and introspective.

clue.text: Examine after an attack -expected to survive

indicators.note: examine comes after the attack, placed second

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
to test is to examine

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a patient over after a seizure and says they will pull through.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin's 'survival of the fittest' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase survival of the fittest, the strongest are those predicted to live on.

clue.text: Girls start with simply designed school tunic

indicators.note: the start of girls is its opening letter
designed means the letters of simply are fashioned into a new form

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls begin with a plainly cut tunic.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymslip is a British school uniform item, a sleeveless pinafore dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pinafore dress worn by schoolgirls, especially in Britain.

clue.text: It sparks off a megaton explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of megaton apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge nuclear blast is set off by something.
explanation.walkthrough: A MAGNETO is a small generator that makes the ignition spark in some engines.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto generates the electrical spark that ignites fuel in engines.

clue.text: Locate unpleasant smell, but this won't cure it

parts.note: to place something is to locate it
BO is short for body odour

explanation.surface: Tracking down a nasty odour, though no remedy will fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: BO stands for body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug, so it cannot heal an illness.

clue.text: A drink or two on the quiet

definitions.text: A drink or two on the quiet

indicators.note: in an across answer the two drinks sit on, next to, the quiet sign

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: a drink or two means the same drink twice over

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone having a secret tipple or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or two' repeats ALE, and both follow P, music's sign for quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-coloured bitter beer, which is exactly a drink one might have quietly.

clue.text: Saw dog's name inside lead

indicators.note: the dog's name goes inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a traditional name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a dog's name tag on its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense and 'lead' like a dog leash; they are a saying and the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a traditional maxim.

clue.text: Permanent dwelling

explanation.definitionFit: Lasting means enduring for ever; and to abide is to live somewhere, so living in a place is residing there.

clue.text: Russian girl in gaol break

indicators.note: break means the letters of gaol are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A young Russian woman escapes from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaol break' suggests a prison escape but rearranges GAOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a common Russian female first name.

clue.text: Joan's taken out a golden retriever

indicators.note: taken out means the letters of Joan's are taken apart and rearranged

parts.note: the name Joan with its s

explanation.surface: Joan has walked her golden retriever dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'golden retriever' is not a dog: Jason retrieved the Golden Fleece in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this hero led the Argonauts to bring back the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Food preparation is part of the service

explanation.definitionFit: A prepared item of food served at a meal; and a plate or bowl from a dinner set of crockery.

clue.text: Request to remain true to type?

definitions.text: Request to remain true to type?

parts.words: Request to remain true to type?
parts.note: sounds like asking someone to stay in character, but is a proofreader's mark keeping printed text unchanged

explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark, Latin for 'let it stand', telling the printer to keep the text as set.

clue.text: Vehicle to move before take-off

explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car; and an aircraft taxis, rolling along the runway before it lifts off.

clue.text: Fresh letters of support?

indicators.note: fresh means the letters of the word letters are made anew

explanation.surface: New letters backing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs that holds up a table top.

clue.text: Investigate cut-back at the colliery

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Looking into job cuts at a coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' looks like spending cuts; 'back' reverses AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look into it closely.

clue.text: Two card-games one may come across

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, the British name for blackjack
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A pair of card games that anyone might stumble upon.
explanation.walkthrough: PONTOON is the British name for the card game blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating bridge on boats is something people cross over, so one may come across it.
